newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian Revoz posts 19.6 pct 96 net rise.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian Revoz posts 19.6 pct 96 net rise.

text.p: Slovenian car producer Revoz, a subsidiary of France's Renault, said on Thursday its unrevised 1996 net profit rose to 900 million tolars ($5.9 million) from 752.2 million the year before.

"Our profit was up mainly because of an increase in our sales. The fact that in September we stopped producing the Renault 5 Clio, which is expensive, contributed much to our sales in 1996," Revoz spokesman Bojan Prosenc told Reuters.
He said Revoz expected its 1996 sales to increase by about 20 percent from 111.2 billion tolars a year ago.
In 1996 Revoz' car production rose to a record 89,229 cars, up from 87,513 in 1995.
The company's market share in Slovenia last year climbed to 26 percent from 25.3 percent in 1995.
"We will try hard to keep our market share of about a quarter in the future, although we know that will not be an easy task with such strong competition here," Prosenc said.
Revoz, which is 54 percent owned by French Renault and 46 percent in state hands, said earlier that some job cuts could be on the cards because of modernisation and the reduction of production costs.
Next year Revoz plans to start producing a new model codenamed X 65 to replace the existing Clio.
Revoz' general manager told a local newspaper that preparation for the new model was likely to cost about $70.9 million and the government was expected to contribute to the investment.
The company refused to reveal any further details about the investment.
-- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 151.8 Slovenian Tolars)
